notes.B47: A. CC capacity is chosen to match flue gas flow and CO₂ emission from a 100 MWth biomass boiler.
notes.B48: B. The biomass CHP is assumed to be equipped with flue gas condensation, hence flue gas is available at 35 deg. C.
notes.B49: C. Heat is supplied as low pressure steam 3-5 bara and [130-150 deg. C).
notes.B50: D. Electricity consumption includes CC plant, flue gas fan work and cooling water pumps, but ID cooling tower, other utilities, heat pumps, CO₂ compression, and liquefaction are not included.
notes.B51: E. Purity given on wet basis. On dry basis purity is >99.95%vol
notes.B52: F. CO₂ pressure at outlet flange. Future processes is expected to deliver CO₂ at higher pressure [save compression work).
notes.B53: G. The CO₂ capture percentage from the flue gas is expected to increase from today's 90% to 95% after 2030.
notes.B54: H. 30% of heat is available at 80 deg. C, 70% is available at 50 deg C. The reported 60 deg C is an weighed average.  Heat pump technology for upgrade of low temp waste heat not included in investment costs.
notes.B55: I. Total retrofit cost including site integration [covering steam turbine modification and coupling to district heating net), utilities, cooling water, CO₂ compression, and liquefaction and owner's costs. Heat pump technology for upgrade of low temp waste heat and interim storage for liquid CO2 not included. CAPEX is expected to decrease by 55% in 2050 as the market develops.
notes.B56: J. If the CO₂ is compressed to 150 bar for pipeline transport instead of liquefaction, the investment costs are reduced by 0.2 mill EUR / [t CO₂ output / hour).
notes.B57: K.  If the CHP is euipped with flue gas condensation to <40 deg C the precooler of the CC plant may be omitted. The CC plant cost can in that case be reduced with 5%.
notes.B58: L. Fixed O&M is taken as 3% of CAPEX.
notes.B59: M. Amine and other smaller consumables as well as waste disposal.
notes.B60: N.  Specific power consumption decrease with time as CO₂ is delivered at increasingly higher pressure from the CC plant. If the CO₂ is compressed to 150 bar for pipeline transport instead of liquefaction, electricity input is 0,1 MWh/t and heat output is 0,16 MWh/t in 2020.
